_about: Thing templates for 1950 (Windward). A THING is something physically out there: wildlife, a drift find, a person at work, a secret. Templates are written once and PLACED by rules on real anchors from the coast data, not at coordinates; the world seed and the day seed (ALIVE-SEA.md thing model, round 1 to 3) choose which exist in a given world and on a given day. This file is DATA ONLY: nothing reads it yet. Every template marks where it comes from (source.kind) and carries invented:true when any part of it is invented. Spoken lines are INVENTED-DIALOGUE, short, for Felix to rewrite by eye.
_spec: games/windward/docs/ALIVE-SEA.md: "Grill: the thing model" (rounds 1 to 3, fields in item 7), "mini quests", "anchoring close-ups", "day and night", "logbook". Linked files (later): quests-1950.json (givers and targets by id), artifacts-1950.json (foundVia: thing ids), rumours-1950.json (teller and target: thing or place ids).

_fields.id: unique, "<category>.<slug>"; stable (the change log keys on template + anchor)
_fields.category: wildlife | people | drift | secret | ashore | gear
_fields.years: [from, to]: the era range the template is valid for (guessed from the sources where possible)
_fields.where: { anchor: anchor type, places?: [name-list ids to restrict it to], spot?: a spot at the place, rule: how it is placed, params?: numbers }. Placement is a fixed function of world seed + day seed + anchor + template (ALIVE-SEA 9).
_fields.density: { chance, cap, areaM, stormBoost? }: rarity per template and a cap per area (ALIVE-SEA 10)
_fields.when: { timeOfDay?, dayType?, weather?, season?, storyPhase? }: arrays; absent means any (ALIVE-SEA 7)
_fields.routine: what it does on its own, in a sentence; movement is its type
_fields.reactions: { tap, approach, anchored }: each { effect, line?, reach? (tap only: small | medium | large, scales with the thing's size) }
_fields.personality: people only: gruff | chatty | shy (quest line variants key on it)
_fields.offers: people only: what hailing may lead to: rumour, errand
_fields.speciesCheck: wildlife only: { status, refs[], note }. status: confirmed-1950 | confirmed-today | not-1950 | not-checked (see _vocab.speciesStatus). A confirmed species makes source.kind grounded instead of invented; invented stays true because behaviour, timing and placement are design. not-1950 narrows years so the template does not spawn in 1950.
_fields.requires: { regular: template id, warmth: friendly | warm }: a secret that a regular reveals once they like you (hidden warmth, ALIVE-SEA 18)
_fields.sighting: { kind, line, drawing }: the logbook entry, first person, short; {place} is filled with the nearest named place; drawing is the silhouette slug
_fields.source: { kind: ported | researched | grounded | invented, refs[], note? }; see _vocab.sourceKinds
_fields.invented: true when any part is invented (source kind grounded or invented); false for ported and researched
_fields.lore: { place, hook, index }: the exact hook in data/island-lore.json (places[place].eras[1950][hook][index])
_fields.storyOwned: true: hand-placed by the story (Britta, the boy, the keeper, the depot clerk, scripted moments); the placement engine never spawns it. Kept so quests can name it and so lore links are tracked.

sourceKinds.ported: taken from existing game code (src/life.js); not invented
sourceKinds.researched: the template is a sourced fact (refs name the source id)
sourceKinds.grounded: INVENTED content that grows from a sourced fact or lore hook (refs name it)
sourceKinds.invented: INVENTED, no source behind it (design idea from ALIVE-SEA.md or ours)

templates.name: Gulls following the boat

where.rule: a dozen gulls trail the boat while it is near land; more near a fishing boat

templates.routine: Wheel and glide behind the stern; peel off when the boat stops.

tap.line: The gulls scatter, shrieking, then settle again.

anchored.line: A few land on the water and sit about, hoping.

sighting.line: Gulls following us in from {place}.

refs: src/life.js: "a dozen gulls that follow the boat" (header comment)

speciesCheck.note: ported from src/life.js; gulls were not part of the species check (they are everywhere on this coast)

templates.name: Gulls perched on sea marks

where.rule: on a buoy top, a cairn or a lighthouse rock (src/life.js perchSpots)

templates.routine: Sit on the mark, preen, watch the water.

approach.line: They lift off a boat-length before you reach the mark.

sighting.line: Gulls on the mark by {place}, one always facing the wind.

speciesCheck.note: ported from src/life.js; gulls were not part of the species check

templates.name: A raft of eiders

where.rule: sea 1.5 to 10 m deep with open water round it, one raft per 150 m cell with chance 0.4, 4 birds (src/life.js raftInCell)

templates.routine: Drift in a loose raft over the shallows, diving for mussels. Drakes white, ducks brown.

approach.line: Inside about 28 m they paddle away, then drift back to the raft centre once you have passed.

anchored.line: After a while they forget you and drift closer.

sighting.line: A raft of eiders off {place}. Soft, low voices.

refs: src/life.js: raftInCell, RAFT_CELL_M = 150, RAFT_CHANCE = 0.4, RAFT_SIZE = 4, fleeOffset, FLEE_DIST_M = 28, FLEE_MAX_M = 16

speciesCheck.note: Resident on the west coast (sv.wikipedia: stannfågel in western Sweden; dialect name "knubbgås" on parts of Västkusten). 1950 was a LOW: the population kept falling into the early 1900s and recovered after spring hunting of sea-ducks was banned in the mid-1950s. The raft numbers are ported from today's code; consider a lower chance for 1950.

templates.name: Eider ducks with ducklings

where.rule: in the lee of a low skerry, near where eider rafts form; replaces the plain raft

templates.routine: A duck leads a line of ducklings along the shore rocks; a "nursery" crèche of several ducks may gather.

tap.line: The mother herds them behind a rock, quick, quick.

approach.line: They bunch up and keep their distance.

anchored.line: One duckling is bolder than the rest and paddles over to look.

sighting.line: Eider ducks with ducklings in the lee of {place}. Eleven, counting twice.

source.note: the SPECIES is sourced (see speciesCheck); its behaviour, timing and placement here are INVENTED design

speciesCheck.note: Same species as the raft (present, at a low in 1950). Early summer is the design; the article does not give a breeding month.

templates.name: Harbour seals hauled out on a skerry

where.rule: a low rock 0.25 to 1.6 m above the sea with water about it, one per 100 m cell with chance 0.3 (src/life.js sealRockInCell)

templates.routine: Lie in a heap on the warm rock, one head up on watch. Slip into the water when something comes close.

tap.line: Splash, splash. Heads pop up further out, looking back.

approach.line: Within about 30 m they slide off one by one (sealDive).

anchored.line: After about a minute of stillness the heads come back, curious.

sighting.line: Harbour seals on a skerry by {place}. Fog lifting.

refs: src/life.js: sealRockInCell, SEAL_CELL_M = 100, SEAL_CHANCE = 0.3, sealDive, SEAL_ALERT_M = 30
docs/ALIVE-SEA.md anchoring grill 5: seals come back after about a minute of stillness
source.note: Species: the county page for Gåsö says knubbsäl, harbour seals (island-lore.json, Gåsö).

speciesCheck.note: Harbour seal (knubbsäl) is Bohuslän's provincial animal and lives along the west coast. 1950: protection began only in the 1970s, so seals were hunted then; present, abundance unknown. The 1988 distemper epidemic is the later event the article stresses.

templates.name: Seal pups west of Storön

where.rule: the seal skerry west of Storön

templates.routine: Mothers guard the pups from the water; the pups lie on the rock.

tap.line: The mothers slip in at once and circle. You feel watched.

approach.line: The mothers slip in well before you are close; the pups stay put.

anchored.line: From far enough away: a pup yawns, and goes back to sleep.

sighting.line: Seal pups west of {place}. Kept my distance. The mothers were watching.

source.note: the lore rumour "The seals west of Storön have pups again" and the boy who counts pups from a rock are INVENTED hooks

refs: lore:relation/10604590 (county page: the seal skerries by Gåsö are a breeding area)
speciesCheck.note: Species sourced; pups in early summer and this skerry are the lore's hook (INVENTED detail on a real breeding area).

templates.name: Cormorants drying their wings

where.rule: on a mark or a bare skerry head, a few birds in a row

templates.routine: Stand with wings hung open like washing, after fishing.

approach.line: One at a time, low over the water, grudgingly.

sighting.line: Cormorants on the mark by {place}, wings hung out to dry.

source.note: "cormorants drying their wings on marks" is an ALIVE-SEA idea

refs: search summary of a Länsstyrelsen Västernorrland report (not read in full): the cormorant re-established as a Swedish breeder at the end of the 1940s, at Kalmarsund
speciesCheck.note: Exterminated from Sweden in the late 1800s; back as a breeder only from the late 1940s on the Baltic side; fast growth in the late 1990s. The shag (toppskarv), the other cormorant of this coast, only became a Bohuslän breeder in 2004. So neither belongs on a 1950 Bohuslän mark. years narrowed to [1990, 2030] so the 1950 engine never spawns it.

templates.name: A heron in the shallows

where.rule: a sheltered shallow shore of a larger island, water under 1.5 m

templates.routine: Stands motionless on one leg; a stab; stands again.

tap.line: It unfolds, slow and enormous, and flaps away over the rocks.

approach.line: It watches until you are very close, then goes.

anchored.line: If you keep still it goes on fishing, ignoring you completely.

sighting.line: A grey heron in the shallows at {place}. Did not move for ten minutes.

source.note: the SPECIES is sourced (see speciesCheck); its behaviour, timing and placement here are INVENTED design

speciesCheck.note: Grey heron is a resident (stannfågel) on Sweden's west coast and a fairly common breeder in the south. 1950 status not in the article.

templates.name: Harbour porpoises

where.rule: outside the skerries, on the Skagerrak side, deep water

templates.routine: A small dark back rolls up, a puff, gone; two or three together, heading somewhere.

tap.line: Too quick: by the time you look, there is only a ring on the water.

approach.line: They surface once, close by, and are gone.

sighting.line: Porpoises, two, outside {place}. Gone as quick as they came.

source.note: the SPECIES is sourced (see speciesCheck); its behaviour, timing and placement here are INVENTED design

speciesCheck.note: The harbour porpoise lives along Sweden's coasts in the Skagerrak and Kattegatt and is the only whale regularly in Swedish waters. The article says a strong decline since the 1960s (citation needed), so it was probably commoner in 1950.

templates.name: A flock diving on a shoal

where.rule: over a shoal of fish, in water a fishing boat would work; draws fishing boats

templates.routine: Gulls and terns fold and drop one after another into the same patch; the water boils faintly.

tap.line: They rise in a cloud and come straight back down.

approach.line: Fish scatter silver at the edge of the patch.

anchored.line: A fishing boat comes to the spot and shouts a greeting.

sighting.line: Birds diving on a shoal off {place}. A fishing boat already on its way.

source.note: the SPECIES is sourced (see speciesCheck); its behaviour, timing and placement here are INVENTED design

speciesCheck.note: Rests on gulls, terns and mackerel, each checked on its own; the behaviour (a flock working a shoal) is the design.

templates.name: Mackerel jumping

where.rule: beside a diving flock or a school, summer evenings

templates.routine: Sudden silver arcs and a patter on the surface.

approach.line: The patter moves away across the water as you come.

sighting.line: Mackerel jumping off {place}. The cutters should know.

source.note: mackerel fishing from Grundsund in this period is sourced; the jumping fish is an INVENTED visual

speciesCheck.note: Mackerel is Bohuslän's provincial fish; it enters the Skagerrak and Kattegatt to spawn in April and May and is fished on the west coast mainly in spring and summer. Grundsund fished mackerel with English-built cutters from the early 1900s. The season is corrected from "late summer" to spring to summer.

templates.name: Terns on a nesting skerry

where.rule: Tärneskär: the name is the tern skerry

templates.routine: A noisy colony: white birds hang in the air, then fold and dive at anything near the nests.

tap.line: A tern dives close past your ear, scolding. Harmless, and very sure of itself.

approach.line: The whole colony goes up, shrieking. Time to keep away.

sighting.line: Terns at {place}, screaming at us to leave. We left.

source.note: the name means tern skerry; that terns nest on it in 1950 is INVENTED

speciesCheck.note: The Arctic tern breeds on coasts and in the outer archipelago along the west coast. That terns nest on Tärneskär in 1950 is INVENTED. The common tern's Swedish range was not found in the article read.

templates.name: Small black birds round the Måseskär lamp

where.rule: circling the lantern in a blow, at dusk or night

templates.routine: Flutter in and out of the beam like moths.

tap.line: Storm petrels, small and black and quick. Käringön folk call them stormtrollet.

sighting.line: Small black birds circling the lamp at {place}. The Käringön folk say they foretell a storm.

refs: people:M10 (storm petrels, Käringön names sjöpink and stormtrollet, believed to foretell storms and carry sailors' souls)

templates.note: The folk belief is people:M10 (Käringön names for the bird); no island-lore hook backs it, so there is no lore link.

speciesCheck.note: People:M10 records Käringön names for the bird and the belief that it foretells storms: that is the 1950-era source. Today it is seen yearly in strong westerlies off Bohuslän; the first one ringed in Sweden was caught on Härmanö huvud in 1988, so it is rare and mostly unseen.

templates.name: Sea sparkle (mareld)

where.rule: any dark water, strongest where the boat or an oar disturbs it

templates.routine: The wake and every oar dip glow green-blue and fade.

tap.line: You trail a hand over the side: sparks run off your fingers.

anchored.line: The boat swinging on the anchor stirs a faint glow all round.

sighting.line: Mareld off {place}. Every oar-dip a handful of sparks.

source.note: the SPECIES is sourced (see speciesCheck); its behaviour, timing and placement here are INVENTED design

speciesCheck.note: Mareld (mostly the dinoflagellate Noctiluca scintillans) is "most common in late summer" (sv.wikipedia). The article is not specific to the west coast or to 1950.

templates.name: Jellyfish drifting

where.rule: in the shallows near villages and harbours, drifting with the current

templates.routine: Pale bells pulse slowly just under the surface.

tap.line: Pretty, and best looked at from the boat.

sighting.line: Jellyfish drifting in at {place}. The bathers will know.

source.note: the SPECIES is sourced (see speciesCheck); its behaviour, timing and placement here are INVENTED design

speciesCheck.note: The moon jelly (called blåmanet on the west coast) is the commonest jellyfish in Sweden; the red lion's mane lives on the west coast. The late-summer timing is the design, not sourced.

templates.name: A fish box

where.rule: afloat in open water; heavier after a blow; stencilled with a port (Grundsund, Käringön, Gullholmen or Lysekil)

templates.routine: Drifts with the wind and current; the same box seen twice will be somewhere else.

tap.line: You hook it with the boathook and lift it aboard. A stencilled name on the end.

sighting.line: A fish box adrift off {place}, stencilled with a port.

refs: docs/ALIVE-SEA.md (lost item template: a fish box)
lore:village:Gullholmen quest seed (a fisherman has lost a fish box in the storm)
source.note: the box and its owner are INVENTED; fish boxes are the right kind of object for a 1950 mackerel coast

templates.name: A lost oar

where.rule: afloat, blade up, usually near a landing or a skerry where someone has been rowing

templates.routine: Drifts with the wind and current; the same box seen twice will be somewhere else.

tap.line: You fish it out. It has been used hard; the loom is worn smooth.

sighting.line: An oar drifting off {place}. Somebody is walking home.

source.note: a drift-find idea from ALIVE-SEA.md ("flotsam from the storm as souvenirs", "a lost oar or fish box")

templates.name: A cork net float

where.rule: afloat in a line or alone, near fishing grounds; sometimes a few still on a bit of rope

templates.routine: Drifts with the wind and current; the same box seen twice will be somewhere else.

tap.line: A cork float, tarred. Some net is missing it.

sighting.line: A cork float off {place}, tarred and salted.

source.note: the drifting float is INVENTED; the cork seine float is in the lore

templates.name: A green glass float

where.rule: bobbing in open water, far from any net; a rare find

templates.routine: Drifts with the wind and current; the same box seen twice will be somewhere else.

tap.line: Green glass, thick, with a seam. It rolls in your hand like a heavy bubble.

sighting.line: A glass net-float adrift outside {place}. Green as bottle glass.

source.note: an invented rare find; glass net floats existed on the Scandinavian coast but this one was not researched for Bohuslän

templates.name: A bottle with a note

where.rule: riding low in the water in a quiet bay or lee

templates.routine: Drifts with the wind and current; the same box seen twice will be somewhere else.

tap.line: A corked bottle with a paper rolled inside, very damp.

sighting.line: A bottle with a note off {place}. The paper points somewhere.

source.note: "A message in a bottle that points somewhere on the chart" is an ALIVE-SEA idea; what the notes say is for the rumour/quest files

templates.name: A crate stencilled with a ship's name

where.rule: after a blow, drifting among broken planks; a ship's name painted on the lid

templates.routine: Drifts with the wind and current; the same box seen twice will be somewhere else.

tap.line: The stencil is half washed off. A ship that lost a deck load.

sighting.line: A crate off {place} stencilled with a ship's name.

source.note: "a crate stencilled with a ship's name" is an ALIVE-SEA idea; the name on each crate is drawn from a short INVENTED list

templates.name: A drifting barrel

where.rule: afloat, stave-built, usually empty; one end stamped

templates.routine: Drifts with the wind and current; the same box seen twice will be somewhere else.

tap.line: Hollow and loud when you knock it. It floats high.

sighting.line: A barrel adrift off {place}. Empty, and glad of it.

refs: docs/ALIVE-SEA.md and GAME-DESIGN.md: pair net sweeps "drifting barrels"
lore:storm-day wrecks with salt, coal, petroleum barrels (ISLAND-LORE.md)

templates.name: A plank from a wreck

where.rule: afloat after a blow, with rusted nails or treenails still in it

templates.routine: Drifts with the wind and current; the same box seen twice will be somewhere else.

tap.line: Oak, black with age. Nails as thick as your finger.

sighting.line: A plank off {place}, with a treenail still in it. From which ship?

source.note: a drifting plank is INVENTED; wrecks and treenails are in the lore

templates.name: A lost pot float with a flag

where.rule: adrift with a short rope and a scrap of cloth for a flag

templates.routine: Drifts with the wind and current; the same box seen twice will be somewhere else.

tap.line: Someone's pot float, lost from its line. The flag is a rag on a stick.

sighting.line: A pot float with a little flag off {place}, cut loose.

source.note: "lobster and pot floats with little flags" is an ALIVE-SEA idea; this is the lost one

templates.name: A tangle of net

where.rule: afloat in a ball of cork floats and knotted twine

templates.routine: Drifts with the wind and current; the same box seen twice will be somewhere else.

tap.line: It takes some hauling. Mostly floats and weed, and a single crab.

sighting.line: A tangle of net adrift off {place}. Somebody will want the floats.

refs: people:Q09 (nets froze stiff in the net box)

templates.name: A child's wooden toy boat

where.rule: drifted from the Käringön pier toward Saltskär, or from the rocks below the dark Stångehuvud light

templates.routine: Floats upright with a stubby mast; the sail is a scrap of sheet.

tap.line: Whittled by someone who loved it. There is a name cut under the keel.

sighting.line: A toy boat adrift off {place}. A child is looking for it.

source.note: both lore quest seeds are INVENTED hooks

templates.name: A small boat adrift

where.rule: a small open boat, unmanned, drifting loose near a landing (src/life.js has a drifting small boat)

templates.routine: Wallows slowly downwind, an oar trailing.

tap.line: No one aboard. Take her in tow, or tell the owner where she went?

sighting.line: An empty boat adrift near {place}. Whose?

refs: docs/ALIVE-SEA.md: "a boat in trouble", "after the squall" quest template
source.note: the drifting boat is ported; its owner and the tow are quest content

templates.name: Pot floats with little flags

where.rule: bobbing in lines along rocky shores in bays and lees; skerries and island shores

templates.routine: A line of floats, each with a little flag; a fisherman hauls them at dawn.

tap.line: Somebody's pots. Leave them be.

approach.line: If you sail right through the line, the fisherman shouts. Not angry, just loud.

sighting.line: Pot floats with little flags at {place}. Sailed round them.

refs: docs/ALIVE-SEA.md: "Lobster and pot floats with little flags in bays; fishermen shout if you sail through"
source.note: ALIVE-SEA notes the lobster season opens in autumn and that date rules changed over the years; not checked for 1950

templates.name: Smoke from the chimneys

where.rule: every village and fishing hamlet, thicker at dawn and dusk

templates.routine: Straight up in calm, flat along the roofs in a westerly: it tells you the wind.

sighting.line: Smoke from the chimneys at {place}, leaning east.

refs: docs/ALIVE-SEA.md: "Life ashore: smoke from chimneys"; "reading the wind: smoke and flags ashore"

templates.name: Washing on the lines

where.rule: between the houses and on the rocks above the quay

templates.routine: Sheets, shirts and long woollen drawers, stiff and flapping.

sighting.line: Washing out on the rocks at {place}. A good drying wind.

templates.name: Nets hung to dry

where.rule: on poles and over fences by the quay; brown tanned nets

templates.routine: Long brown curtains of net, with cork floats in a row along the top.

tap.line: Tarred and cutch-brown. Every hole has been mended twice.

sighting.line: Nets hung to dry at {place}.

source.note: the scene is INVENTED from the sourced fishing life

templates.name: Church bells on a Sunday

where.rule: carries across the water to a boat within about 500 m

templates.routine: Rings the hour of service, once each Sunday morning.

sighting.line: Church bells carrying across the water from {place}. A Sunday.

refs: people:Q12 (Fiskebäckskil church 1772 with votive ships; Grundsund church 1799)

templates.name: A dog barking on the quay

where.rule: a working quay in a village; one dog, tied or free

templates.routine: Barks at every boat that comes close, then loses interest.

tap.line: Wag, wag.

approach.line: A bark, then a second, politely.

sighting.line: A dog on the quay at {place}, barking us in.

where.rule: every automatic (AGA) light in the window that is lit, one by one as the sun valve closes

templates.routine: The black rod cools, the valve opens, the flame catches: no one is there to see it.

templates.name: A fisherman out at dawn, home at dusk

where.rule: leaves the home harbour at first light and returns at dusk with gulls behind

templates.routine: Out through the gap at dawn, working the grounds, home at dusk with the catch and a cloud of gulls.

lines.hail: Birds are working off the point. Go and see.

sighting.line: A fishing boat heading out of {place} at first light, gulls already behind her.

refs: docs/ALIVE-SEA.md day/night grill 5: "fishermen out at dawn, home at dusk"
